summary: These changes improve video decoding and display across Linux and Android. On Linux, HDR frames now use the standard shared-memory image path instead of direct DMA-BUF uploads (a way to share GPU buffers), while Vulkan Video keeps the H.264 DRM format details needed by some older NVIDIA drivers; decoded image bounds are also adjusted to match scaling. On Android, the AImageReader setting is clarified and unused SurfaceTexture canvas handling is removed, with no user-visible feature change expected.
